About the Role: Own and execute the Country Risk dimension of the Group ERMF — the third face of the 3 Dimension risk model (Product × Function × Country). The role is accountable for country-level risk visibility across all licensed jurisdictions: defining regional risk reporting, developing country-specific financial and fraud risk indicators, reducing ERM implementation gaps in the regional dimension , and acting as the central risk team's primary interface with regional GMs, Risk Officers and Regional MLROs.

The role closes the gap between a centrally designed framework and locally varying business models, so risk is detected at country level early enough to act on.

Scope

• Geographic: All licensed and licensed-pending jurisdictions. Tiered by licence type, revenue materiality, business model complexity and regulatory intensity.

• Risk types: Primarily financial (credit, market, liquidity) and non-financial (fraud risk) at country level, plus operational, outsourcing and conduct risk as they manifest regionally.

• Decision rights: Recommends country risk ratings, KRI thresholds and escalations; approves regional risk report content; owns country risk log integrity.

What You’ll Do:

• Design and maintain the regional risk assessment methodology: risk report, taxonomy mapping, country risk rating criteria, country risk register standard.

• Set jurisdiction tiering and proportionate reporting requirements per tier.

• Translate Group ERMF and respective risk policies into regional implementation guidance.

• KRI development and monitoring: Develop country-level KRI suites for financial and non-financial risk; extend from pilot markets to all licensed regions.

• Own KRI definitions, thresholds, escalation triggers and review cadence; recalibrate annually and on material business change.

• Operate the regional risk dashboard and automated monthly reporting, with AI-assisted interpretation for local teams and senior management.

• Assess KRI breaches; drive closure through regional Risk Officers and functional owners with documented root cause and remediation.

• Reporting and governance: Produce the periodic Regional Risk Report: risk profile, KRI performance, emerging risks, incidents, remediation status by jurisdiction.

• Prepare and present regional risk content to the Risk Management Work Group, regional Risk & Compliance Committees and Board-level reporting where required.

• Regional risk dashboard operationalised as a working tool: automated data feeds live, threshold alerting and escalation triggers functioning, and regional teams self-serving — evidenced by reduced manual intervention and a measurable fall in reporting cycle time.

• Maintain the country risk log; track issues to closure with named owners and dates.

• Support regulator engagement on cross-border and regional matters alongside entity Heads of Risk, Compliance and Legal.

• Primary point of contact of Group risk for regional GMs, Risk Officers and MLROs.

• Run regional risk forums; convert business-model-specific insight into KRIs and scenario content.

• Drive Risk 101 and risk culture initiatives into regional populations.

What We’re Looking For:

• Degree-level qualification in Risk Management, Finance, Economics, Accounting, Law, Mathematics, Engineering, or another relevant field.

• 7+ years in risk management, with meaningful time in regulated financial services or crypto/digital assets.

• Track record building KRIs, risk registers and risk reporting from scratch, not just operating an existing framework.

• Sufficient grounding in prudential/financial risk (capital, liquidity, credit, market) and non-financial (Operational, fraud, etc.) to define meaningful country-level indicators.

• Experience engaging and influencing GM/CEO-level stakeholders without direct authority.

• Demonstrated experience interacting with regulators, Boards, senior management, and other key stakeholders.

• Strong analytical capability, with excellent communication, influencing, and stakeholder management skills. Multi-jurisdiction, multi-regulator experience — essential.

• Forward-looking risk leader with the ability to connect regulatory expectations, business strategy, and practical risk controls.

• Strong decision-maker who can assess complex issues, form clear views, and provide constructive challenges in a fast-moving environment.

• Credible and confident communicator, able to engage effectively with regulators, Boards, senior management, and cross-functional teams.

• Strong ownership mindset, with a disciplined approach to governance, documentation, escalation, and follow-through.

• Comfortable working in a high-growth, highly regulated environment where standards, processes, and controls continue to evolve.

• Naturally curious about financial markets, digital assets, market structure, and emerging risk themes.

• Strong analytical writing — turns data into a clear risk narrative for executive and board audiences.

About the Team:
We are looking for an experienced software engineer to join our System Security team and build the tools and platforms that make secure software delivery the default, starting on the developer's machine. You will work across the full path code takes, from local development through source control, dependencies, and CI/CD to production artifacts, and make sure that only trusted code, built by trusted pipelines, reaches production.

Security starts where code is written. You will shape the local developer experience: the CLIs, Git workflows, package managers, dev environments, IDE integrations, and AI coding assistants engineers use every day. Your job is to make that toolchain both fast and hardened. That means credentials that never need to sit on disk, dependencies that are vetted before they are installed, secrets caught before they are committed, and local tools that cannot be quietly turned against the developer. Done well, the secure path is also the fastest path, so engineers choose it on their own.

From there, you will carry the same principle through the rest of the chain. You will design pipeline templates and platform services that give every team secure defaults, and solve hard systems problems along the way: short-lived credentials and workload identity for every pipeline, trusted dependencies, and artifact integrity from build to deploy. Strong security guarantees have to coexist with low latency, high reliability, and a developer experience engineers actually like.

You'll join at a time of high impact. Our delivery platform runs [X,000+] pipelines a day for [N00+] engineers across GitHub Actions, Jenkins, and an in-house CI. AI-assisted development and coding agents are increasing both the speed of delivery and the volume of change flowing through these systems, on laptops as much as in CI. Securing that without slowing engineers down takes strong engineering and great tooling, not more process.

What You'll Do

• Build and own the developer CLI and local toolchain integrations, such as Git credential helpers and hooks, so that secure access to code and services is the default and the fastest option.

• Harden the local development environment: vetted package installs, safe defaults for package managers, dev containers or reproducible environments, and controls for IDE extensions and AI coding assistants.

• Shift security feedback all the way left: pre-commit secret and dependency checks that are fast, accurate, and easy to fix.

• Build reusable, secure-by-default pipeline templates, plus a CLI that lets teams adopt them in minutes.

• Design and build platform services that sit in the critical path of software delivery and are fast, reliable, and hard to bypass.

• Bring OIDC workload identity and short-lived credentials to CI/CD, so that pipelines get only the access they need, only for as long as they need it.

• Add signing, provenance, and SBOM generation to every build, and enforce verification and policy at deploy time.

• Design dependency controls, such as proxies, pinning, and allow/deny policies, that block malicious and typosquatted packages without breaking builds.

• Harden CI/CD against pipeline injection, untrusted third-party actions and plugins, and runner compromise.

• Build security signals into the tools developers already use, including PR checks, CLI feedback, and clear fix guidance, so that problems are caught before merge.

• Measure adoption and developer friction, and use the data to improve the paved path.

• Partner with platform, infrastructure, and product teams, and take part in incident response.

What We’re Looking For:

• 5+ years of software engineering experience, with strong Go or Python (Rust or Java also welcome) and the ability to build and run production services on your own.

• Experienced building developer tooling, internal platforms, or infrastructure that sits on the critical path of software delivery.

• Strong understanding of how Git, GitHub, and CI/CD systems (GitHub Actions, Jenkins) work internally, including their trust boundaries and common attack paths.

• Hands-on experience with at least one of: artifact or image signing, provenance/SBOM, OIDC workload identity, secrets management, or dependency security.

• Familiar with a major public cloud, Kubernetes, and containers.

• Product-minded: you design for the developer first, and you can drive adoption through good tooling rather than mandates.

We understand not everyone will meet every qualification on day one. If this work excites you, we encourage you to apply.

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.




THE TEAM

 

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

 

Kraken Prop, launched in 2026 inside Kraken Pro, lets traders prove their skill in a simulated evaluation and then trade funded capital of up to $200,000, keeping up to 90% of the profits. There are no time limits on evaluations, no consistency rules and no profit caps, and payouts are typically processed within 24 hours.



We are looking for an Affiliate Growth Lead, US to build and scale our relationships with trading-focused creators and affiliates across the US market. The role combines business development, creator and affiliate partnerships and performance marketing, with a clear commercial mandate: drive attributable evaluation purchases and repeat engagement on Kraken Prop.



This is not a crypto-native KOL role. The audience we want to reach already trades, studies trading, or is actively looking for a path to trading capital, and we reach them through the creators, educators and publishers they trust. Many of them already follow prop-firm and funded-trader content in futures, forex and index trading.



 


THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own business development for US trading creators and affiliates, building a high-quality pipeline of trading educators, prop-firm and funded-trader YouTubers and streamers, podcasters, newsletter authors, trading community and Discord operators, and established prop-firm affiliate publishers.

 - Develop and execute the US creator and affiliate strategy for Kraken Prop, focused on driving evaluation purchases and repeat purchases, with the scope to expand across other Kraken Pro products such as spot, margin and futures.

 - Own partner acquisition and relationship development, from initial outreach and commercial conversations through activation and ongoing growth.

 - Structure revenue-share and hybrid partnerships that tie partner incentives to evaluation purchases and funded-trader activity, not clicks or sign-ups alone.

 - Set up and manage the tracking, attribution, payout and reporting needed to measure partners from click through evaluation to repeat purchase.

 - Work with Legal and Compliance on disclosure, content review and approved messaging, so that promotion of Kraken Prop is accurate and consistent.

 - Partner across Growth, Marketing, Product, Kraken Prop and other relevant teams to turn creator and affiliate opportunities into effective campaigns, and bring partner and trader feedback back into the product.

 - Continuously identify emerging creators, communities and affiliate publishers that reach aspiring and active traders in the US.

 
 
 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Deep experience in business development, partnerships, influencer management or affiliate-led growth in the US, with a track record of running performance-based creator or affiliate programs for a prop trading firm, brokerage, trading platform or trader-education product.

 - Experience growing prop-firm, funded-trader, evaluation-based, futures, forex or other active-trading products, and an understanding of how those programs convert and retain customers.

 - A strong existing network and understanding of the US trading creator ecosystem, including trading educators, prop-firm and funded-trader content creators, finance YouTubers, streamers, newsletter authors, podcasters and trading community operators.

 - Working knowledge of crypto and digital assets, with the ability to explain Kraken Prop clearly to audiences who are new to crypto or to Kraken.

 - Demonstrated ability to originate, negotiate and grow commercially meaningful partnerships, including revenue-share and hybrid deal structures.

 - Hands-on experience with affiliate networks and tracking platforms.

 - Familiarity with US financial advertising rules, and experience getting creator content through compliance reviews.

 - Strong relationship-building skills, with the credibility to work with creators who protect their audience's trust and are selective about the brands they promote.

 - Commercial judgment: you prioritize partners based on expected impact on purchases and repeat engagement, not on reach or activity alone.

 - Comfort using performance data to evaluate partners, diagnose results, adjust strategy and end partnerships that do not perform.

 - Strong cross-functional execution skills and the ability to move opportunities from prospecting through launch and ongoing growth.

 



Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.




OUR COMMITMENT

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.


We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.


As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

We've built an AI-native localization stack: agentic translation workflows that already publish content with minimal human touch. The translation agent itself works. What decides whether it scales is everything around it — the terminology assets that keep it consistent, the automated testing that catches what it breaks in the live product, and the evaluation infrastructure that tells us when it can be trusted to publish without a human.

That surrounding platform is what this role owns.

This is a genuine bridge role, and we mean both halves. You bring localization domain depth — you know what makes a translation wrong, what breaks in-product, how terminology and locale rules actually work — and the AI product instinct to turn that judgment into agents, metrics and automated tooling. You will define what "good" means, build the systems that measure it automatically, and make our human experts dramatically more leveraged.

What You’ll Be Doing

• Own the terminology and glossary system that ensures consistent localization across markets and product surfaces, including term proposal, approval, versioning, integration into agentic workflows, and compliance monitoring.

• Build agent-driven tools that scan live mobile and web experiences to identify localization issues that translation review alone may miss, such as text truncation, layout defects, hardcoded strings, unlocalized imagery, and incorrect number, date, or currency formats.

• Deliver the MVP for automated localization auditing and evolve it into localization testing embedded within internal product-testing infrastructure, enabling issues to be caught automatically before release.

• Define and operate the translation quality gate for human-free publishing, supported by golden datasets, standardized error-classification annotation tools, automated evaluation, and quality metrics.

• Balance automation coverage against content risk across announcements, Help Center content, and product UI; investigate systemic gate failures, identify root causes, and drive improvements back into the localization agents.

• Integrate annotation workflows with internal AI infrastructure, enabling linguists to provide standardized, real-time feedback that continuously improves agent performance.

What We Look For In You

•

5+ years in product management, including ownership of backend or infrastructure systems that business operations run on — not only user-facing surfaces.

•

Localization or translation domain depth. You can look at a translation and say precisely why it's wrong, and you understand terminology management, locale rules and what breaks when content meets a real UI.

•

Shipped AI/ML or evaluation-driven products, including internal tooling. You partner with AI teams as a peer rather than consuming their output.

•

Strong data fluency. You define metric frameworks for fuzzy, subjective quality problems and turn them into measurable, automatable systems — and you reason clearly about precision/recall trade-offs, such as false-flag rate vs. miss rate.

•

Excellent cross-functional execution across engineering, AI, design and external partners, in a multi-market, multi-language, multicultural environment.

Nice to Haves

•

LLM evaluation and eval-driven development: eval harnesses, golden datasets, prompt and QE design, tuning against gold sets, and reading failure modes well enough to tell a prompt problem from a data problem from a model problem.

•

Hands-on experience with TMS platforms such as Phrase or Smartling, and i18n standards (ICU/CLDR).

•

Bilingual in English and Chinese.

•

Transcreation, marketing localization or brand voice adaptation across markets.

•

Content systems experience — CMSes such as Contentful or Webflow — or familiarity with design tooling such as Figma.

•

Crypto, fintech or another high-compliance regulated domain.

Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

Job Description
As a Compliance Officer - Onboarding, you will be part of the Compliance Department and work in the Compliance Onboarding, Reviews & Advisory Team.
Your responsibilities will be primarily focused on Onboarding related matters and the associated Advisory role. You will also be working in close collaboration with the Reviews team and contribute to the mission of the Compliance Department, acting as a second line of defense.
Key responsibilities
Onboarding
• Conduct ex-ante reviews of all account opening requests involving High-Risk Relationships (HRR) clients and Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) (private clients, corporate structures such as, but not limited to, operating, domiciliary companies, trusts, collective investments schemes, external asset managers, as well as financial institutions), prior to account activation:
• Assess the overall client onboarding file and its supporting documentation, conducting due diligence verifications as required
• Review the HRR memorandum prepared by the first line of defense (1LoD) in order to submit a recommendation to the Executive Management (EM) and/or the relevant AML decision-making body
• Be able to defend the Compliance position within the relevant AML decision- making body
• Work in close coordination with the Business Risk Management (BRM) or Client Lifecycle Integrity (CLI) departments, which are part of the first line of defense
Reviews
• Conduct ex-ante reviews of periodic/ongoing reviews involving High-Risk Relationships (HRR) clients and Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) (private clients, corporate structures such as, but not limited to, operating, domiciliary companies, trusts, collective investments schemes, external asset managers, as well as financial institutions)
• Assess the supporting file and the review materials prepared by the 1LoD and submit recommendations for EM approval.
• In addition to the assessment to be performed for onboarding requests, periodic review requests require a transactional activity analysis of the file.
Advisory & Support
• Provide advisory support to the BRM, CLI, Front Office departments regarding account opening requests requiring Compliance input as well as general Compliance matters
• Provide guidance on complex questions arising both from the internal compliance framework and external regulatory requirements
• Provide guidance on the application of the risk tolerance framework as defined by the Board of Directors to the BRM and CLI teams
• Contribute to drafting, and optimizing, internal memos and procedures
• Participate in key regulatory projects
• Contribute to providing AML training sessions to the Front Office, BRM and CLI departments

Qualifications
Qualifications
• Bachelor or Master Degree, preferably in Laws or in Economics
• Minimum 5 years of experience in client onboarding, KYC/AML, or compliance within the financial sector
• Strong Knowledge of Swiss regulatory framework (AMLA, AMLO-FINMA, CDB) and other applicable regulations
• Strong knowledge of onboarding due diligence standards
• Excellent command of English and French (another language is a strong asset)
• Ability to multi-task and work under pressure
• Analytical and methodological approach
• Very good communication skills
• Strong team player who enjoys working in multicultural, dynamic, technological and international environment

Job Description
1. Campaign build, management and account health
• Build and upload campaigns and assets across Search, Performance Max, Demand Gen, YouTube and App campaigns using the platform UI and Google Ads Editor.
• Manage assigned campaigns and markets day to day, including settings, targeting, bids, budgets, optimisation goals, ad copy and asset updates.
• Execute fast, accurate bulk builds, bulk edits and structural changes in Google Ads Editor.
• Maintain account hygiene through naming conventions, labels, URL checks, disapproval checks, pre-launch QA, change logs and regular health reviews.
• Identify and implement optimisation opportunities without prompting, including bid-strategy changes, bid adjustments, channel or placement exclusions and wider account-health actions.
• Use Google Asset Studio where appropriate to create practical asset variations; ownership of full creative production remains with the creative team.
2. Search-term and keyword analysis
• Implement scripts and AI tools integrations to review search-term data regularly to identify irrelevant traffic, emerging demand, new keyword opportunities and changes in user intent.
• Implement scripts and AI tools integration to build and maintain negative keyword coverage at the appropriate account, campaign and ad-group level.
• Implement scripts and AI tools integratio to expand and refine keyword portfolios using query evidence, performance and market-specific search behaviour.
• Assess match-type performance, query quality, duplication and routing to improve relevance and control.
• Translate findings into clear actions across keywords, ad groups, copy, landing pages, bids and campaign structure.
3. Budget pacing and forecasting
• Monitor spend against approved market and campaign plans, maintaining an accurate pacing view.
• Flag over- or underspend risk early, explain the cause and recommend corrective action.
• Reallocate budget within agreed guardrails based on performance, delivery opportunity and business priority.
• Provide short-term spend forecasts and month-end outlooks, clearly stating assumptions and delivery risks.
• Escalate material budget, tracking or inventory constraints before they affect delivery.
PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT
4. Creative and asset performance
• Analyse ad and asset performance by campaign, market, audience, format and funnel stage where data is available.
• Identify winning and underperforming hooks, messages, propositions, calls to action, formats and variations.
• Convert performance findings into clear test hypotheses and prioritised recommendations.
• Brief the creative team on new concepts, copy directions and asset variations, including the objective, audience, insight, message, format, required versions and success metric.
• Track new assets from briefing through launch and post-test analysis, documenting learning for future iterations.
• Maintain sufficient asset variety and refresh cadence to support Search, Performance Max, Demand Gen, YouTube and App activity.
5. Landing-page performance
• Monitor post-click performance and conversion rates using available analytics, segmented by campaign, keyword or query, audience, device, market and landing page where useful.
• Identify likely friction points, message mismatch, weak intent alignment, broken journeys or page-performance issues that may suppress conversion.
• Check destination URLs and campaign-to-page alignment as part of launch and ongoing QA.
• Brief CRO, web or product teams on evidence-based landing-page test opportunities; this role supports analysis and briefing rather than owning the full CRO roadmap or page development.
• Evaluate landing-page test results alongside media metrics to determine whether changes improve both conversion efficiency and traffic quality.
6. Competitor monitoring
• Monitor observable competitor search presence, messaging, offers, claims and landing-page approaches in priority markets.
• Track material changes that may affect impression share, click costs, brand defence, generic performance or user expectations.
• Summarise findings without presenting estimated competitor activity as confirmed fact.
• Turn competitor observations into practical recommendations for keyword coverage, copy, offers, landing pages, bidding or structured tests.
7. Structured testing
• Maintain a prioritised test backlog across ads and assets, keywords and match types, bidding, campaign settings, audiences and landing pages.
• Define a clear hypothesis, control and variant, primary success metric, guardrails and expected decision before launch.
• Configure Google Ads experiments or other agreed test designs, validate setup and protect data quality during the test.
• Interpret results with appropriate caution, distinguish directional findings from conclusive results and document limitations.
• Record outcomes, decisions and next actions so learnings can be reused across markets.
• Support incrementality and lift tests through configuration, QA and data collection under the direction of the PPC lead or measurement team.
DELIVERY, MEASUREMENT AND GOVERNANCE
8. Tracking and measurement
• Maintain working knowledge of conversion tracking across front-end and server-side events.
• Validate Google Ads tags and diagnose broken, missing, duplicated or misfiring conversions; no full GTM setup ownership is required.
• Support implementation, validation and troubleshooting of Enhanced Conversions and Enhanced Conversions for Leads.
• Work with analytics or MarTech partners to resolve tracking issues and confirm that optimisation signals remain fit for purpose.
• Understand the relationship between platform conversions, downstream quality and value metrics, and flag material discrepancies.
9. Reporting and analysis
• Run weekly analysis for assigned markets and identify the main performance drivers, blockers and risks independently.
• Produce clear, concise reporting covering performance versus target, budget pacing, material changes, areas of focus and planned optimisations.
• Move beyond descriptive commentary by translating analysis into prioritised recommendations, owners and next actions.
• Use spreadsheets confidently for pivots, lookups, reconciliations and large platform exports.
• Maintain clear documentation for tests, budget changes, structural changes and material optimisation decisions.
10. Multi-market delivery and agency QA
• Optimise multi-language accounts with appropriate consideration of local copy, keywords, search behaviour and market nuance.
• Coordinate translations and local validation where needed; do not rely on unreviewed machine translation for market-facing copy.
• Turn around agreed ad hoc market requests to deadline while protecting planned priorities.
• QA agency output in assigned markets against agreed build, tracking, compliance and reporting standards.
• Escalate conflicts in market priority, resource or deadline risk promptly.
11. Compliance and governance
• Monitor and resolve ad and asset disapprovals, escalating policy or legal questions through the correct internal route.
• Maintain advertiser verification and certification status where required.
• Follow approved claims, disclaimers, landing-page and market restrictions, and maintain an auditable record of material changes.
• Apply disciplined pre-launch and post-launch QA, including naming, targeting, budgets, bidding, URLs, assets, conversion goals and policy status.
12. Ways of working
• Communicate proactively with the line manager on progress, blockers, decisions and deadline risk.
• Organise concurrent market priorities effectively and deliver to agreed timelines.
• Collaborate effectively with creative, CRO/web, analytics, MarTech, compliance and agency partners while retaining clear ownership of PPC execution.
• Stay current with relevant Google Ads product changes and apply new capabilities only where they support agreed objectives and controls.

Qualifications
• 3+ years of hands-on paid search experience, ideally in a high-competition or complex vertical.
• Proven delivery across Google Ads Search, Performance Max and Demand Gen, with practical exposure to asset-led campaign management.
• Advanced working ability in Google Ads Editor, including bulk builds, bulk edits and structural changes.
• Strong search-term and keyword-management capability, including negative keywords, match types, query-quality analysis and keyword expansion.
• Ability to manage campaigns and identify and implement account optimisations independently.
• Practical budget pacing and short-term forecasting skills, including early identification of over- or underspend risk.
• Strong performance-analysis skills and the ability to produce actionable weekly reporting.
• Ability to analyse creative and asset performance and brief new concepts or variations to a creative team.
• Ability to assess landing-page performance and brief evidence-based improvements without requiring full CRO ownership.
• Working knowledge of conversion tracking, Google Ads tags and GTM troubleshooting; full GTM setup is not required.
• Strong spreadsheet skills, including pivots, lookups and handling large data exports.
• Structured testing mindset: clear hypotheses, success metrics, reliable setup, careful interpretation and documented learning.
• Clear written communication for senior reporting and partner briefs.
• Disciplined QA, documentation and change-control habits.
• Deeper experience across Demand Gen, YouTube and App campaigns.
• Microsoft Advertising platform and Editor experience.
• AppsFlyer or an equivalent mobile measurement partner, including event mapping, attribution windows and familiarity with SKAN.
• Experience advertising financial services under Google's restricted-category requirements, including advertiser verification, certification and claims that may trigger disapprovals.
• Multi-market and multi-language account-management experience.
• GA4 and Looker Studio experience.
• Experience using Google Ads experiments and interpreting inconclusive or directional results appropriately.
• Awareness of AI-led search developments, including AI Max and account structures that support algorithmic bidding.
• Experience using auction, market or competitive-insight tools to support observable competitor monitoring.
• Experience working with downstream value or quality signals, mobile attribution or value-based bidding.
• Experience with building scripts and utilization of AI tools to automate workflows.

Additional Information
IN SCOPE

Hands-on build and optimisation; search-term and keyword management; budget pacing; reporting; creative and landing-page analysis; briefs to specialist teams; test execution; tracking diagnosis; campaign QA; disapproval management; and multi-market delivery.
NOT THE PRIMARY OWNERChannel strategy, full creative production, the CRO roadmap, website development, full GTM implementation, legal or policy interpretation, advanced measurement design, or final cross-market budget strategy. The specialist contributes evidence and executes agreed actions in these areas.

Capital Com UK Limited (CCUK) is an FCA (MIFIDPRU) investment firm that operates a UK CFD and spread betting platform. The Finance Manager role was created to address two needs simultaneously: to add senior-level capacity at a moment when the UK Finance team is supporting a concentrated programme of strategic projects and to raise the maturity of the control environment in preparation for an increasingly rigorous external audit cycle. You will be the Finance Director's deputy — covering Board, ExCo, and governance forums when required — and will have one direct report (Management Accountant). You will also play a leading role in embedding AI and automation into Finance's operating model, reducing time spent on routine processing and creating space for higher-value analytical work


Responsibilities
Financial Control & Reporting

Own the month-end close process end-to-end: review journals, sign off balance sheet schedules, manage accruals and prepayments, and oversee AP and expense processing carried out by the group's shared services function on CCUK's behalf.

Prepare first-draft management accounts and produce the Monthly Director's Analysis (MDA) pack, including P&L actuals vs budget, variance commentary, and commercial KPI narrative.

Prepare annual statutory financial statements for CCUK under IFRS and act as the primary Finance contact for the external statutory auditor throughout the year-end process.

Design and document the CCUK financial controls framework: process narratives, control matrices, and risk-and-controls documentation aligned to Big Four audit standards. This should be aligned with the Finance Risk and Controls Self Assessment (RCSA).

Tax

Own UK corporation tax compliance: prepare quarterly provisions, coordinate with external advisers on the CT600 return, and manage tax considerations arising from new product lines (Stockbroking, Cards).

Manage quarterly VAT returns, including the partial exemption calculation that arises from CCUK's mix of VAT-exempt CFD/spread betting income and taxable supplies.

Maintain transfer pricing documentation for intercompany service charges received and work with the Tax team to ensure this is kept up to date.

Treasury

Oversee CCUK's treasury function: maintain daily cash positioning across banks, PSP, and EMI accounts in Kyriba, ensure daily reconciliations are completed and reported on time, manage banking counterparty relationships, and ensure FX exposure is monitored and hedged via the group's intercompany hedging structure.

Ensure client money segregation remains compliant with CASS 7 at all times, working closely with the dedicated CASS team on treasury-related aspects of the daily CASS checklist.

Regulatory Capital & Governance

Support FCA regulatory reporting: contribute to quarterly RegData submissions (capital adequacy, liquidity, P&L, balance sheet) and ICARA documentation, with a view to taking greater ownership of these processes over time.

Act as Finance Director cover: represent CCUK Finance at Board, ExCo and ARCC Committee meetings when required, and step in across any part of the Finance function in the FD's absence.

People & Automation

Manage and develop one direct report (Management Accountant): set clear objectives, conduct regular 1:1s, and build the team's capability in financial controls and analytical output.

Qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent) with post-qualification experience at an FCA-authorised firm — investment management, stockbroking, spread betting, banking, or fintech.

Strong IFRS technical knowledge and the ability to prepare statutory financial statements, develop accounting policies, work through complex accounting treatments, and document conclusions clearly for audit purposes.

Practical FCA regulatory reporting experience: ICARA, RegData submissions, and a working knowledge of the UK Investment Firms Prudential Regime (UK IFR / MIFIDPRU), including capital adequacy and liquidity monitoring.

Working knowledge of CASS 7 (client money segregation) and the obligations it places on an FCA (MIFIDPRU) investment firm.

The Technical Support Manager retains authority for staffing, leave, formal performance reviews and disciplinary decisions. Designated leads own incident command, specialist recovery and root-cause analysis.

Review shift performance against agreed GTS measures for response and resolution SLA attainment, first-contact resolution for eligible incidents, employee satisfaction (CSAT), escalation timeliness and the quality of tickets and handovers. Report exceptions, actions and owners to the Technical Support Manager. Follow up with the assigned resolver on cases transferred to another team.

Work rostered shifts, including weekends and public holidays where applicable, under the published rota and agreed employment terms. The vacancy specifies location, employing entity and onsite requirements. Assigned duties follow the agreed GTS and IT Operations ownership model.

Job Description
Campaign build, management and account health
•
Build, launch and maintain campaigns across Meta, TikTok and X for web conversion, lead generation, app install and app-event objectives.
•
Manage assigned campaigns and markets day to day, including objectives, optimisation events, audiences, placements, bids, budgets, schedules, creative, copy and destination settings.
•
Execute accurate campaign duplication, bulk changes and asset uploads using available platform tools and approved workflows.
•
Monitor delivery and diagnose issues including limited learning, low delivery, audience saturation, frequency pressure, placement inefficiency and conversion-signal weakness.
•
Maintain account hygiene through naming conventions, labels, URL and UTM checks, disapproval checks, pre-launch QA, change logs and routine health reviews.
•
Identify and implement optimisation opportunities independently within agreed commercial and compliance guardrails.
Audience strategy and analysis
•
Build and maintain prospecting, retargeting and lifecycle audience structures aligned to campaign objectives and customer journey stages.
•
Use approved first-party, website, app-engagement and platform audiences, including custom audiences, lookalike or equivalent expansion and automated audience products where appropriate.
•
Maintain accurate exclusions and suppression logic to reduce overlap, protect prospecting activity and avoid inappropriate retargeting.
•
Analyse audience performance by market, funnel stage, creative and placement; identify saturation, weak quality, scale constraints and expansion opportunities.
•
Turn audience findings into clear actions across targeting, exclusions, budget allocation, creative briefs and campaign structure.
Budget pacing and forecasting
•
Monitor spend against approved plans by platform, market and campaign, maintaining an accurate pacing view.
•
Flag over- or underspend risk early, explain the cause and recommend corrective action.
•
Reallocate budget within agreed guardrails based on performance, delivery opportunity, downstream quality and business priority.
•
Provide short-term forecasts and month-end outlooks, clearly stating assumptions and delivery risks.
•
Escalate material budget, tracking, policy or inventory constraints before they affect delivery.
Creative performance and briefing
•
Analyse performance by creative concept, hook, message, proposition, format, duration, placement, call to action and variation where data is available.
•
Identify winning and underperforming patterns, creative fatigue and gaps in platform-native asset coverage.
•
Convert findings into clear test hypotheses and prioritised recommendations rather than descriptive commentary.
•
Brief the creative team on new concepts, iterations and platform-native variations, including objective, audience, insight, hook, message, format, required versions and success metric.
•
Track assets from briefing through launch and post-test analysis, documenting learning for future iterations and localisation.
Landing-page and post-click performance
•
Monitor post-click conversion performance using available analytics, segmented by platform, campaign, audience, creative, device, market and landing page where useful.
•
Identify likely friction, message mismatch, weak journey alignment, broken links, tracking gaps or page-performance issues that may suppress conversion.
•
Check destination URLs, deep links, app-store routes, UTMs and campaign-to-page alignment as part of launch and ongoing QA.
•
Brief CRO, web, product or app teams on evidence-based improvement and testing opportunities; this role supports analysis and briefing rather than owning the full CRO roadmap or development.
Competitor monitoring
•
Monitor observable competitor advertising, messaging, offers, creative formats and landing-page approaches across priority markets.
•
Use public platform ad-transparency and creative-discovery resources, alongside market observations, to identify material shifts and testable themes.
•
Turn observations into practical recommendations for messaging, creative formats, audience hypotheses, landing pages or structured tests.
Structured testing
•
Maintain a prioritised test backlog across creative, audiences, placements, bidding and optimisation, campaign structures and landing pages.
•
Define a clear hypothesis, control and variant, primary success metric, guardrails and expected decision before launch.
•
Configure platform experiments or other agreed test designs, validate setup and protect data quality during the test.
•
Interpret results carefully, distinguishing directional evidence from conclusive findings and documenting limitations.
•
Record outcomes, decisions and next actions so learning can be reused across platforms and markets.
•
Support conversion-lift, brand-lift and incrementality studies through setup, QA and data collection under the direction of the paid social lead or measurement team.
Tracking and measurement - web and app
•
Maintain working knowledge of platform pixels/tags, event configuration and server-side or conversion API concepts relevant to Meta, TikTok and X.
•
Validate conversion events and diagnose broken, missing, duplicated or misfiring signals; deep engineering implementation remains with Analytics or MarTech.
•
Work with Analytics and MarTech partners on event mapping, data quality, attribution settings and optimisation-signal readiness.
•
Use AppsFlyer or an equivalent mobile measurement partner for app campaign setup and analysis, including event mapping, attribution windows, deep links and app-event optimisation.
•
Understand privacy-related app measurement concepts, including SKAdNetwork, and flag material discrepancies between platform, MMP and backend reporting.
Reporting and analysis
•
Run weekly analysis for assigned markets and identify key performance drivers, blockers, risks and opportunities independently.
•
Produce concise reporting covering performance versus target, budget pacing, funnel and quality signals, material changes and planned optimisations.
•
Provide actionable creative, audience, placement, platform and landing-page insights with clear owners and next actions.
•
Use spreadsheets confidently for pivots, lookups, reconciliations and large platform exports.
•
Maintain clear documentation for tests, budget moves, structural changes and material optimisation decisions.
Multi-market delivery and agency QA
•
Execute and optimise multi-market and multi-language campaigns with appropriate consideration of local audience behaviour, creative conventions, copy and compliance nuance.
•
Coordinate translations and local validation where needed; do not rely on unreviewed machine translation for market-facing copy.
•
Turn around agreed ad hoc requests to deadline while protecting planned priorities.
•
QA agency output in assigned markets against agreed build, tracking, creative, compliance and reporting standards.
•
Escalate conflicts in market priority, resource or deadline risk promptly.
Compliance and governance
•
Monitor and resolve ad and asset disapprovals, escalating policy or legal questions through the correct internal route.
•
Follow approved claims, disclaimers, targeting restrictions, landing-page requirements and market rules, maintaining an auditable record of material changes.
•
Apply disciplined pre- and post-launch QA covering naming, objective, audience, exclusions, placements, budgets, schedule, optimisation event, URLs, tracking, creative and policy status.
Ways of working
•
Communicate proactively with the line manager on progress, blockers, decisions and deadline risk.
•
Organise concurrent market and platform priorities effectively and deliver to agreed timelines.
•
Collaborate with creative, CRO/web, app, analytics, MarTech, compliance and agency partners while retaining clear ownership of paid social execution.
•
Stay current with relevant changes across Meta, TikTok and X, applying new automation and AI-led capabilities only where they support agreed objectives and controls.

Qualifications
Essential skills and experience
•
2+ years of hands-on paid social experience, ideally in a high-competition or complex vertical.
•
Proven day-to-day campaign delivery across Meta, with practical hands-on execution across TikTok and X.
•
Experience managing both web and app acquisition campaigns, including optimisation to conversion and app events.
•
Ability to build, QA, launch, optimise and troubleshoot campaigns independently across concurrent markets.
•
Strong audience-management capability across prospecting, retargeting, first-party/custom audiences, expansion, exclusions and saturation analysis.
•
Ability to analyse creative performance and brief new concepts, iterations and platform-native variations to a creative team.
•
Practical budget pacing and short-term forecasting skills, including early identification of over- or underspend risk.
•
Experience designing and interpreting structured tests across creative, audiences, placements, optimisation and campaign setup.
•
Ability to assess landing-page and post-click performance and brief evidence-based improvements without requiring full CRO ownership.
•
Working knowledge of paid social conversion tracking, event validation and troubleshooting across web and app.
•
Strong performance-analysis and written-reporting skills, with the ability to convert data into prioritised actions.
•
Strong spreadsheet skills, including pivots, lookups, reconciliations and handling large data exports.
•
Disciplined QA and governance approach covering naming, URLs, tracking, audiences, budgets, creative, policy status and change logging.
•
Clear written communication for reporting upwards and briefing internal teams, agencies and external partners.
•
Proactive workload management, ownership of deadlines and early escalation of blockers or risk.
Desirable skills and experience:
•
Experience advertising financial services or another regulated category across Meta, TikTok or X, including policy restrictions, verification and disapproval resolution.
•
Experience managing multi-market and multi-language paid social accounts.
•
AppsFlyer or equivalent MMP experience, including app-event mapping, deep links, attribution windows and SKAdNetwork concepts.
•
Practical exposure to platform pixels, server-side measurement or conversion APIs, working with Analytics or MarTech teams on implementation and troubleshooting.
•
GA4, Looker Studio, Power BI or comparable analytics and reporting experience.
•
Experience supporting conversion-lift, brand-lift or incrementality studies and interpreting results appropriately.
•
Experience using public ad libraries or creative-discovery tools for structured competitor and creative monitoring.
•
Understanding of downstream quality, value-based optimisation or predictive customer-value signals.
•
Experience QAing agency work or coordinating delivery across internal and external partners.
•
Working knowledge of current platform automation and AI-led campaign products, with sound judgement on when to use or constrain them.

Additional Information
Role boundaries:
•
This is a hands-on channel-execution role, not ownership of the overall paid social or cross-channel strategy.
•
The role owns creative analysis, test recommendations and performance-led briefing; the creative team owns full concept development and production.
•
The role identifies landing-page and journey issues and briefs tests; CRO, product, web and app teams own their roadmaps and implementation.
•
The role validates and troubleshoots tracking and coordinates fixes; Analytics, MarTech or engineering own deep technical implementation.
•

BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE


Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.




THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

Consumer Growth builds mobile and web experiences that help people become Kraken customers, fund their accounts, invest, earn, access new products, build wealth and stay lifelong clients. Product, engineering, design, data, and lifecycle marketing build together.




THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Choose the right bets. Identify the client segments and problems worth solving. Own the roadmap and allocate effort against expected client value, commercial impact, and engineering cost. Set the baseline, target, and threshold for scaling; stop weak bets.

 - Build NTU retention. Help newly transacting users build on their first transaction, discover further value, and form repeat investing and financial habits through their first weeks and months. Find where they stall and improve the steps that lead to lasting use.

 - Retain and bring back established clients. Keep active clients engaged, address signs of lapsing, and reactivate clients who have stopped. Understand how needs change with tenure, holdings, and financial goals, then deepen the client’s relationship with Kraken.

 - Make the next financial move useful. Test ways to support client intent: recurring deposits and buys, useful portfolio context, timely opportunities, or relevant Earn products. Choose from the evidence. Successful automated investing and Earn can create lasting value without frequent manual activity. Make rewards, access, and risks clear.

 - Prove the commercial impact. Track retention by cohort and segment, linking behavior to retained balances, net inflows, product adoption, and revenue. Measure active engagement through useful actions, such as reviewing a portfolio or investing, and track successful automated habits separately. Distinguish inflows from asset-price gains, establish incremental impact, account for incentives and costs, and check that gains last after promotions end.

 - Connect product and lifecycle. Partner with lifecycle marketing on push, email, web, and app journeys, from a relevant message to a useful financial action. Adapt to local payment habits and market requirements.

 - Build and ship with the team. Turn the chosen problem into prototypes, requirements, and experiments with engineering, design, and data. Bring risk, compliance, and legal partners into design decisions. Balance client impact, reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed; scale what works.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - Evidence that you’ve personally led consumer product changes that beat retention or expansion targets. Be ready to explain the baseline, target, result, timeframe, and your contribution, including the impact on revenue, assets, or retained balances.

 - A clear account of what changed underneath the result: component behaviors or funnel rates such as repeat deposits, return-to-transaction conversion, successful recurring investments, or reactivation. Show how you established incremental impact and whether it lasted.

 - Strong client and product judgment. You can choose a segment and problem worth pursuing, understand why clients return, hold, withdraw, or disengage, and turn that insight into a useful experience.

 - Hands-on analytical depth. You query and validate your own data, diagnose cohorts and funnels, size opportunities, and design experiments that can detect a commercially meaningful effect.

 - Commercial discipline. You can explain how market conditions, incentives, costs, and client trust affected your results, and use that evidence to decide whether an improvement is worth scaling.

 - Senior ownership from decision through delivery. You’ve owned a roadmap, made product and technical trade-offs, allocated effort, stopped weak bets, and worked effectively with engineering, design, data, lifecycle marketing, and risk/compliance partners.




NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience with consumer investing, wealth, savings, fintech, or crypto products. Freemium gaming is nice-to-have as well.

 - Experience building recurring investment, deposit, Earn, portfolio, or goal-based experiences.

 - Experience adapting client journeys across markets and local financial behaviors.







Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.




OUR COMMITMENT

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.


We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.


As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

Connect on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/kraken-exchange/

Responding to all incoming client queries through live chat or telephone in a timely and professional manner.

To develop proficient product knowledge with an understanding of pricing and business rules.

Company Description
In the fast-growing economies of the world, there's a new generation of ambitious younger people eager to gain financial independence and we’re here to make this potential a reality by empowering them with the Freedom to Succeed.
We empower them with guidance, tools, and easy market access so they can trade and invest with confidence. We aim to make our clients their own wealth manager: empowered to create investment strategies and make investment decisions effortlessly, in their own time, on their own terms, in their own way.
Founded in 1998 to offer online trading for retail clients, the Exinity Group is now over 25 years old and has provided leveraged trading to over 2 million customers through our global power brands, including FXTM and Nemo, giving them access to equity, commodity and FX markets across the Middle East, Asia, and Africa.
Exinity is an energetic and diverse company with central offices in the UAE, Cyprus and the UK, plus a number of smaller hubs globally. We’re always looking for talented individuals to join us. ‘Freedom to Succeed’ is not just a promise we make to our clients and partners, but to our people too. We’ll help you develop a range of skills, take on early responsibility, and enjoy a rewarding and fulfilling career with a fast-growing, dynamic company.

Job Description
Do you get a genuine thrill from finding the tool, the template or the workflow that makes an entire team faster overnight? Can you look at a static design or a piece of motion and immediately see how it should flex by market, by language, by audience, without anyone having to rebuild it from scratch every time? Then this might be the most exciting role we're hiring for right now.
We're creating a brand-new role, Creative AI Technologist / CMP Specialist, sitting within the Design pod, with a genuinely dual mandate. Half the role is owning our Creative Management Platform: building dynamic templates across image, video and rich media that let a small in-house Creative team punch well above its weight, producing hundreds of localised, on-brand ad variants across six very different brands without anyone burning out doing it by hand. The other half is bigger than any one platform: you'll be the person driving AI and automation adoption across the whole Creative team, bringing tools like Claude for design and code, alongside our CMP’s own AI capability and whatever comes next, into everyday production.
This is a rare chance to shape how an entire creative function works, not just execute inside it. You'll have real license to experiment, pilot new tools, kill the ones that don't earn their place, and champion the ones that do, across Copy, Design and Motion alike. If you get excited talking about what AI could do for a creative team rather than just what it does for you personally, we want to talk.
What You'll Do
•
Own our CMP end to end: template architecture, feed/data-driven creative setup, user administration and platform best practice, across both static and motion formats.
•
Build modular, dynamic ad templates, including display, social and video/motion, from approved design concepts that scale cleanly across brands, markets, languages and funnel stages.
•
Champion AI and automation adoption across the Copy and Design pods, introducing tools such as Claude for design and code, and evaluating new AI tools as they emerge.
•
Build and share practical workflows, prompts and templates that let colleagues use AI tools confidently in their own work, not just watch you use yours.
•
Set up and manage the data feeds (pricing, promos, market data, localisation strings) that drive dynamic variants, working with Performance Media on what needs to flex and why.
•
Be the technical go-between for Creative, Performance Media/Ad Operations and any external production or media partners on dynamic and programmatic creative builds.
•
QA every build against network specs (Meta, Google, programmatic display, TikTok and more) before it goes live; you're the last line of defence before creative ships across dozens of markets at once.
•
Document the systems and workflows you build, and train Copy pod colleagues and fellow designers to use them confidently, so none of it lives in your head alone.

Qualifications
Qualifications and Experience
•
Hands-on experience with a Creative Management Platform, working across both static and motion/video formats.
•
Genuine, hands-on experience using AI tools in a creative or production context, such as Claude, generative design or code tools, or similar; this is essential for the role, not a bonus.
•
A track record of bringing new tools or workflows into a team and getting real adoption, not just personal use.
•
A background that blends design or motion skills with a genuinely technical, systems-minded approach to production.
•
Working knowledge of HTML5/CSS for banner and dynamic ad builds, and comfort working in templates and components rather than one-off static files.
•
Experience in financial services, trading or fintech advertising is an asset, particularly across multiple regulated or offshore markets, but isn't essential.
The Type of Person We're Looking For
•
Genuinely excited by what AI and automation can do for a creative team, not just personally curious about the tools.
•
A natural evangelist and teacher, who'd rather upskill five colleagues than be the only person who knows how something works.
•
A first-class communicator who can translate between designers, copywriters and media buyers without losing anyone.
•
Has the rigour and attention to detail to work in a highly regulated sector, where a wrong spec or stray line of copy actually matters.
•
Organised and comfortable owning a platform that the rest of the team depends on.
•
Thrives in a fast-paced, multi-brand, multi language environment and enjoys solving the same problem for multiple audiences at once.
•
Can share examples of dynamic, templated or AI-assisted creative work you've built, static or motion, and ideally examples of tools or workflows you've helped others adopt.

Who we are

We simplify wealth creation. Founded in 2014 in Vienna, Austria by Eric Demuth, Paul Klanschek and Christian Trummer, we’re here to help people trust themselves enough to build their financial freedom — for now and the future. Our user-friendly, trade-everything platform empowers both first-time investors and seasoned experts to invest in the cryptocurrencies, crypto indices, stocks*, precious metals and commodities* they want — with any sized budget, 24/7. Our global team works across different cultures and time zones, bringing our products to more than 7 million customers, making us one of Europe’s safest and most secure platforms that powers modern investing.

Headquartered in Austria but operating across Europe, our products are built by fast-moving, talented, “roll-up-your-sleeves-and-make-it-happen” kind of people. It’s these diverse perspectives and innovative minds operating as ONE TEAM that keep Bitpanda at the cutting edge of our industry. So if you’re someone who thinks big, moves fast and wants to make an impact right from day one, then get ready to join our industry-changing team. Let’s go!

Your mission

As a Senior Product Manager at Bitpanda, you will take end-to-end ownership of key product areas and strategic pillars, scaling our offerings for financial institutions, banks, and strategic partners. Operating in a high-impact, complex, and regulated environment, you will define product strategy, shape the roadmap, and act as a key sparring partner to Product Leadership.

You will work closely within a collaborative structure, allowing you to focus deeply on product architecture, scalability, and technical execution while leveraging client-facing insights to inform your roadmap. This is a global, fast-paced role requiring seamless context-switching across markets, products, and evolving regulatory frameworks.

What you'll do

• Take end-to-end ownership of core product pillars, defining the long-term vision, strategy, and execution roadmap in close alignment with Product Leadership.

• Partner with Engineering to translate complex market and partner needs into clear, actionable, and scalable technical capabilities.

• Work closely with Client Solution Leads—and engage directly with external partners when needed—to weigh client-specific requests against long-term platform scalability and strategic priorities.

• Proactively integrate fintech and financial services regulatory requirements into the product lifecycle, collaborating closely with Compliance and Legal to ensure every launch meets global standards.

• Act as a central connector across Engineering, Sales, Client Solutions, Legal, and Compliance, managing senior stakeholders and driving clarity amid ambiguity and shifting priorities.

Who you are

• Proven track record managing B2B and/or B2B2C products within finance, banking, fintech, or crypto.

• Demonstrated experience operating as a Senior Product Manager or Lead Product Manager, with end-to-end ownership of complex products.

• Solid understanding of regulatory requirements in fintech or financial services, with hands-on experience shipping compliant products in highly regulated environments.

• Ability to partner effectively with engineering teams, break down technical trade-offs, and build scalable, platform-level solutions rather than one-off customisations.

• Comfortable thinking globally, switching contexts rapidly across multiple product pillars, and navigating evolving priorities in a dynamic environment.

• Strong communication skills with the ability to align senior internal stakeholders and engage credibly with institutional partners when required.

What’s in it for you

• Flexibility to work where you thrive – Enjoy the freedom of our Hybrid working model, combining onsite collaboration and remote work, with an additional 25 days per year to work from a city or country of your choice.

• Reward for your impact – Receive a competitive total compensation package aligned with Bitpanda’s pay-for-impact policy, including participation in our stock option plan.

• Support for your mental wellbeing – Access confidential coaching, counselling, and mental health resources whenever you need them through OpenUP.

• Time to recharge – On top of your standard annual leave, prioritise your wellbeing in 2027 with 3 additional days of paid time off to rest, reset, and recharge, available once you’ve been with us for 6 months.

• Continuous learning and growth – Grow your skills and stay ahead in your career with unlimited access to Udemy’s library of online courses at your own pace.

• Exclusive perks and rewards – Enjoy discounts, rewards, and perks from partners worldwide across lifestyle, wellness, tech, and travel.

• Support during life milestones – Take advantage of up to 8 additional weeks of gender-neutral new parent leave to welcome and bond with your new addition to the family.

• Fuel and focus on-site – Pandas in Vienna, Bucharest, Barcelona, and Berlin can enjoy free onsite dining, with freshly prepared lunches and snacks to keep you fueled and focused all day long.

• Recognition for your contributions – Celebrate milestones and achievements with recognition and rewards for your Tenure at Bitpanda.

• Show your Bitpanda pride – Access exclusive Bitpanda-branded merchandise and gear to represent.

• Connect and celebrate with your team – Join unforgettable company events, from our Winter Party in Vienna to gatherings worldwide, fostering fun, connection, and celebration

.…and even more location-specific benefits designed to make life at Bitpanda even more rewarding wherever you are.

Above all, you will have the opportunity to learn and grow as part of Bitpanda’s incredible journey towards being Europe’s future #1 investment platform.

Bitpanda is committed to fostering a fair and equal environment based on trust and mutual respect. We believe that a diverse and inclusive workplace is paramount to our success and we are committed to building a team that represents a wide variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills.

* These benefits may be adjusted at Bitpanda’s discretion and do not apply to our internships and exceptions to our Hybrid Working policy apply to teams with shift schedules or for folks whose roles require them to be in-office (think: Workplaces team or IT).

You’ll run intake for the New Product Capital Assessment (NPCA) and New Product Approval Process (NPAP), learn how each product and business actually works, work with our Quant team to turn that understanding into rigorous capital calculations, and make sure the results are documented, repeatable, and ready for auditors and regulators. You care as much about how a product affects our clients as about how it affects our balance sheet.

 - Coordinate sign-offs across Product, Engineering, Quant, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Treasury, and Finance, escalating blockers early

 - Keep a complete audit trail of assumptions, approvals, and open items for every product reviewed

 - Map each new launch to applicable regulatory and prudential requirements with Legal and Compliance

 - Keep methodology documentation, control evidence, and process records current

 - Hands-on experience running operational processes, such as product approvals, change management, or regulatory reporting, with clear controls and documentation

 - Solid grasp of capital and RWA concepts (Basel, CET1, liquidity and reserve requirements) and the ability to work through calculations and challenge model outputs

 - Comfort working with Quants and engineers, including reading methodologies and assumptions, and asking sharp questions

 - Ability to learn products and business models quickly, and explain their risk and client impact in plain language

 - Understanding of crypto-specific risks, including smart contracts, oracles, settlement finality, stablecoins, tokenization, and DeFi mechanics

 - Working knowledge of the regulatory environment for crypto, stablecoins, and tokenized assets

 - Strong project and program management skills, and the ability to drive consensus and deadlines across many teams

 - Proficiency in Excel and SQL; Python a plus

   - Set up monitoring and alerts for tracking breakages, fraud and volatility-driven spikes in traffic and conversions, such as sharp market moves, and escalate per policy.
   
   - Participate in cross-functional discussions with product, compliance, finance, design, data and performance marketing, and prioritise requests openly.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - Hands-on experience with web and mobile attribution, including MMPs (such as AppsFlyer or Branch), SKAN, deep linking and web-to-app journeys.

 - Understanding of why ad platforms credit conversions differently, and experience with conversion APIs and server-side tracking for Meta, Google Ads and TikTok.

 - Comfortable working with data: SQL and a data warehouse, able to read an event schema and trace a discrepancy back to its source.

 - An AI-native way of working: you already use AI assistants and agents day to day for analysis, SQL, scripting, documentation and automation, move fast with them, check their output before relying on it, and follow our data privacy and security rules when doing so.

 - Experience working within safety and compliance practices in a regulated environment, such as consent and financial promotion rules, and monitoring data and alerts through volatile periods when traffic and conversions swing quickly.

 - Strong stakeholder management and written communication skills, with experience aligning performance marketers, engineers, data, finance and compliance around a number they might not align on.

 - Able to write a clear spec, work with engineers to deliver it and review the result.

 - Detail-oriented and process-driven, able to manage multiple workstreams and prioritise the problems that move spend decisions.

 - Genuine interest in the crypto or fintech industry.




NICE TO HAVES

 - Exposure to incrementality testing or marketing mix modelling.

 - Experience building AI-assisted workflows or lightweight automations, for example with LLM APIs, scripts or agents, for reporting, QA or monitoring.

As OKX continues to expand its products, markets and investment activities, we are looking for a Global Tax Business Partner at Senior Manager level to join our lean, high-impact tax team. The role will partner closely with Product, Finance, Legal, Compliance and Operations teams, to provide commercially practical tax advice, support informed decision-making and ensure that material tax considerations are addressed early and implemented effectively.

What You’ll Be Doing

•

Act as the primary tax business partner for the Group’s business globally including its CeFi, Web3, investment arm businesses, building strong relationships with Business, Product, Finance, Legal, Compliance and Operations teams

•

Develop a strong understanding of each business’s products, operating model, fund flows and growth priorities to identify tax considerations early in the decision-making process

•

Partner with the finance BP to determine tax implications of new products, listings, licensing initiatives, new fiat rails and various other initiatives

•

Coordinate the assessment of direct tax, indirect tax, withholding tax, transfer pricing, permanent establishment, nexus and tax-reporting implications, working with Group Tax specialists and external advisers as required. This role owns the business interface: identifying tax issues early, framing commercial options, escalating to the right internal or external SME, and driving approved positions into implementation.

•

Translate complex tax issues into clear commercial implications, practical options and recommendations that enable stakeholders to make informed decisions

•

Work with finance transformation team to establish appropriate tax review gates for material products, transactions and operating-model changes etc and ensure that all material products, listings and market entries receive documented tax sign-off before launch

•

Support the design and implementation of commercially practical and technically supportable entity, contractual, transaction and fund-flow arrangements

•

Work with Finance, Legal, Product, Operations and tax specialists to ensure approved tax positions are implemented consistently in legal agreements, systems, processes, data and accounting treatment

•

Monitor relevant tax legislative, administrative and enforcement developments and proactively assess their impact on the Group’s businesses and planned initiatives

•

Maintain a business tax risk register and documentation of material tax positions, decisions and assumptions, ensuring that identified risks are escalated and remediated on a timely basis

•

Contribute to process improvement initiatives, including enhancement of tax intake processes, documentation standards, knowledge sharing and the use of technology, data analytics or AI in tax workflows

•

Undertake any other tasks and projects assigned.

What We Look For In You

•

10+ years of relevant international tax experience, ideally with a mix of Big 4 or advisoryand in-house roles

•

Broad technical grounding across international tax, permanent establishment and nexus, withholding tax, transfer pricing and indirect tax, with the judgement to identify when specialist advice is required

•

Proven business partnering experience, including advising on new products, transactions, investments, operating-model changes or market-entry initiatives;

•

Strong understanding of commercial and operational considerations, with the ability to translate complex tax issues into practical options and balanced recommendations

•

Experience in digital assets, fintech, financial services, asset management, venture capital or another highly regulated or transaction-driven business is highly preferred

•

Familiarity with crypto is a strong advantage

•

Strong stakeholder-management and communication skills, including the ability to influence senior stakeholders and coordinate cross-functional teams without direct authority

•

Strong analytical and project-management skills, with keen attention to both detail and the bigger picture and the ability to manage multiple priorities across jurisdictions and time zones

•

Self-starter, comfortable operating with ambiguity in a fast-paced, start-up-like environment; resourceful, adaptable and collaborative

•

Demonstrated ability to manage external advisers and drive recommendations through to implementation

•

Familiarity with tax technology, data analytics or AI applications in tax processes is a plus.

Perks & Benefits

•

Competitive total compensation package

•

Various team building programs and company events

•

Wellness and meal allowances

•

Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

•

More that we love to tell you along the process!
